title: Arabic
description: Modern Standard Arabic, written right to left with transcription: greetings, family, food, numbers, travel and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: Arabic is written from right to left. 'السلام عليكم' (as-salamu 'alaykum) is a common greeting; the reply is 'وعليكم السلام' (wa 'alaykum as-salam).

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
tips: Adding ـي (-i) to a noun means 'my': 'أم' (umm, mother) becomes 'أمي' (ummi, my mother).

units.title: Food and drink
tips: 'ال' (al-) means 'the'. Before some letters its sound blends into the next one: 'الشاي' is said ash-shay.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
tips: Both Western digits (1, 2, 3) and Arabic-Indic digits (١ ٢ ٣) are used in the Arab world.

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
tips: 'من فضلك' is said min fadlak to a man and min fadliki to a woman - the spelling is the same.

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
tips: Many words change for men and women: a man says 'أنا ذاهب' (ana dhahib), a woman 'أنا ذاهبة' (ana dhahiba).

units.title: Shopping
units.description: Ask for things, prices and how to pay.
tips: 'أريد' (urid) means 'I want'; add 'من فضلك' (min fadlak) to make it polite.
